title: Little Rock at Sam Baker's: short pay, a pawned bass drum and heating the head
summary: At Sam Baker's in Little Rock he was paid $5 instead of $14 to cover the previous drummer's debt, and had to warm his bass drum by a stove.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: stand so we could go and play at Sam Baker's.
He had the joint in Little Rock where we played.

Yes, and we supposed to get $14 a week and I worked 3 weeks before Basie gave me $5, and I pulled out my pistol and I was going to shoot everybody. I had a bass drum that I had to haul off the band and go over to a great big pot-bellied stove to heat it up so it could tighten up so I could finish the dance. (laughter)
About what size? You guys go by sizes in bass drums.
It was about a 26 by 5 but I couldn't get the pliers to tighten it up.
So you put the heat on it.

Heat... They stopped the band, hold up the whole dance, and go over and tie my drum around it to heat it up, now we could play again. I had a cymbal that's like a pot, pan, and skillet and Jimmy Rushing used to sit around and say, "That sounds good..." these instruments
And I didn't understand why this man was supposed to give me $14 and I worked 3 weeks and they gave me $5. I said, "What is this?" He said, "Well, you took

Mac's place and he took $25 and you have to pay his debt." I died! You see, Milt, in those days when you joined the band nobody told you nothing. When you took another man's place, you were him, and if he owed anything, fine. But what had happened, I didn't know. I had left them and they took a job for a week, a place called - oh, I don't know the name now. Jimmy Rushing wouldn't draw any money because he's going to get his money at the end of the week. But Chick the guitar player Jake and the saxophone player had tabbed all the whiskey and at the end of the week the man said, you ain't got nothing coming. Oh, Milt - (laughter)
